report_name: SETTRA Ransomware Group Hits Israel's Largest Car Importer

threat_actors.name: SETTRA
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that conducted a double extortion cyberattack against Colmobil, Israel's largest vehicle importer. The group encrypted data, exfiltrated sensitive information, and demanded a ransom.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: SETTRA exfiltrated sensitive data, including customer personal details, before deploying the ransomware for encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: SETTRA deployed its ransomware to encrypt files on Colmobil's network, disrupting business operations.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The ransomware group likely deleted volume shadow copies or backups using tools like vssadmin.exe or wbadmin.exe as a precursor to encryption.

malware.name: SETTRA Ransomware
malware.description: Ransomware used by the SETTRA group to encrypt files on Colmobil's network as part of a double extortion attack.

tools.name: vssadmin.exe
tools.description: A legitimate Windows tool likely used by the SETTRA group to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

tools.name: wbadmin.exe
tools.description: A legitimate Windows tool likely used by the SETTRA group to delete backups to inhibit system recovery.

identities.name: Colmobil
identities.description: Israel's largest vehicle importer, targeted by the SETTRA ransomware group in a double extortion attack.

identities.name: Hyundai
identities.description: A vehicle brand imported by Colmobil. Mentioned as context for the victim's business.

identities.name: Mercedes-Benz
identities.description: A vehicle brand imported by Colmobil. Mentioned as context for the victim's business.

identities.name: Mitsubishi
identities.description: A vehicle brand imported by Colmobil. Mentioned as context for the victim's business.

identities.name: Israeli Ministry of Transport
identities.description: A government agency that was forced to sever its connection with Colmobil due to the cyberattack.

indicators.name: Suspicious Shadow Copy Deletion via Vssadmin or Wbadmin
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Shadow Copy Deletion via Vssadmin or Wbadmin
id: f6c2d1e0-a3b4-4f5e-8d9c-0123456789ab
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe or wbadmin.exe to delete shadow copies or system state backups, a common TTP for ransomware groups to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/c3qzmnfiw
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-29
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_vssadmin:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete shadows'
  selection_wbadmin:
    Image|endswith: '\wbadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete catalog'
      - 'delete systemstatebackup'
  condition: 1 of them

indicators.name: Suspicious Execution of Vssadmin or Wbadmin
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious Execution of Vssadmin or Wbadmin
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of vssadmin.exe or wbadmin.exe, which can be used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery. This is a generic detection and should be correlated with other suspicious activity.
references:
  - https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/c3qzmnfiw
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-29
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\vssadmin.exe'
      - '\wbadmin.exe'
  condition: selection
